newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France to increase some ex-Europe rates Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: Air France to increase some ex-Europe rates Oct 1.

text.p: Air France said it will be increasing its ex-Europe rates by between five and ten percent, from October 1, on routes where market demand is strong.

"While we are not prepared to go into details on rates increases to specific destinations, the best performing routes for us at present are to the Far East, South America and French -speaking Africa," said Air France Cargo's vice-president Europe, Jean-Luc Servant.
"Overall, rates are stable with no particular downward pressures in evidence," he added.
Servant described the current state of the ex-Europe market as stable.
He said France was generating a satisfactory level of demand as was Germany,Italy and Scandinavia. The UK market was expanding, he added, which is in contrast to Spain which was stagnant.

"Quite honestly,it is difficult to know what course the market will follow in the last quarter of the year. A dominant feature at present is the buoyant level of spot quotations we are dealing with for shipments of five tonnes and above. However, this provides little indication on how the market will look a few months from now."
